% Pattern: attach/nested. A head "Proof of (i)" inside a proof is a part of
% that proof, and proves what it proves. Seen in the gold pilot (set X).
% want proposition-1 statement/proposition 1.1
% want proof-1 proof - proves=proposition-1
% want head-1 proof - proves=proposition-1
% want head-2 proof - proves=proposition-1
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\newtheorem{proposition}{Proposition}[section]
\begin{document}
\section{One}

\begin{proposition}
(i) Every finite group has a composition series. (ii) Any two have the
same length.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
We follow the usual route.

\noindent {\bf Proof of (i):} Take a maximal normal subgroup and go on.

\noindent {\bf Proof of (ii):} Compare two series by refinement.
\end{proof}
\end{document}
